A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same initialization study for spline-based Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks. Text, equations, Tables 1–5, Figures 1–23, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original function-fitting, forward-PDE, and Feynman benchmark results, together with training curves, grid searches, and NTK analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally displays LeCun NTK spectra in several appendix comparisons.

M1.justification: The LeCun-numerical, LeCun-normalized, Glorot-inspired, and power-law initialization procedures remain unchanged. Section 3.1 retains the same normalization and weight-scaling formulas.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five two-dimensional functions, Allen–Cahn, Burgers and Helmholtz PDEs, and 20 dimensionless Feynman formulas. The added NTK panels concern existing tasks and scenarios.

E2.justification: Appendix F.3, Figures 18–22, adds LeCun-numerical to the displayed NTK comparisons for f1, f2, f4, f5, and Burgers. Those plots previously displayed only baseline, Glorot, and power-law results, although Figure 22's caption already named LeCun. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Architecture configurations, training budgets, sampling procedures, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Sections 3.2 and 4.2 and Appendix C. The additional spectra use the existing large-architecture setting; no revised evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Figures 18–22 extend the existing training-dynamics analysis with LeCun spectra at initialization, intermediate iterations, and convergence, including both Burgers residual and boundary-condition kernels. The exponent-sensitivity and learning-rate-scheduling analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds except three for the power-law grid search, median benchmark outcomes, and averaged training curves with standard-error bands. No new uncertainty-reporting practice or run-count change appears.

E6.justification: The LeCun NTK curves in Figures 18–22 are newly reported result entries. Numerical values in Tables 1–4 are identical, and the main performance rankings and other reported benchmark findings are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are retained, including the initialization derivations in Appendices A–B and the RBA-weighted NTK derivation in Appendix F.1. Citation and footnote formatting changes do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a systematic study of spline-KAN initialization, benefits from Glorot in parameter-rich architectures, and the strongest overall performance from power-law initialization. The replacement abstract closing sentence restates the existing contribution rather than introducing a new claim.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning variance preservation, PDE derivative scaling, NTK conditioning, and learning-rate oscillations are retained. Section 5.1 preserves the limitations concerning power-law theory, domain coverage, and transferability.

D1.justification: The JAX/jaxKAN implementation, RTX 4090 hardware, optimizer and sampling details, and code/data/seed access statement remain. Removing the duplicate repository sentence from the abstract does not change the access information retained in the Reproducibility Statement.

R1.justification: The same 33 cited works and research positioning are retained. Alphabetical reference ordering, expanded author names, and reassigned Wang 2025a/2025b labels are bibliographic changes to matched works.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the abstract's closing sentence, revises the funding acknowledgment, and adds an LLM Usage paragraph disclosing grammar and syntax assistance. Citation style and reference ordering change, while the scientific prose and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR format throughout, changing headers, margins, typography, title/author presentation, and figure/table placement. Figures 18–22 expand from three to four comparator columns, the Feynman tables occupy separate pages, and Figure 16 now shares a page with the Appendix F.2 discussion.

improvement.justification: The added LeCun panels make the existing NTK comparisons more complete and resolve Figure 22's mismatch between its caption and displayed methods. This improves the inspectability of the diagnostic evidence. The gain is limited because the method, benchmark scores, theoretical arguments, and limitations remain unchanged.
